runtime.source: locally built binary from the working copy that adds a compaction retained-tail patch to official v2.1.1; the patch touches no plugin API, event schema or hook
runtime.note: Stock OpenCode 2.1.1 is accepted and self-checked, not qualified: no stock 2.1.1 binary was run here.

qualification.basis: Isolated native OpenCode 2.1.1-compaction.1 process with synthetic loopback providers (bridge/opencode/protocol-smoke.mjs, protocol-ws-smoke.mjs, protocol-hot-reload-smoke.mjs, protocol-compaction-smoke.mjs). Temp HOME, temp config, loopback fixture. No real model, no inference, no cloud account, no live configuration.
qualification.schemaReview: Compared tag to tag, v2.0.32 to v2.1.1: every name and field the companion reads is unchanged, including the session hook names and their provider filter, the request kinds primary/compaction/title/generate, the x-opencode-session-id request header, the event envelope and subscription, the step/text/reasoning/tool/execution events and tokens.output/tokens.reasoning. 2.1 changed only how a summary compaction stores what it keeps (metadata.keepID on the checkpoint, materialized as metadata.recent by session.context), renamed optional providerState to native, and added session.archived/session.unarchived. None of those is read here.

acceptanceRule.note: A locally built runtime is accepted only by reviewed identifier, never by suffix pattern, so an unreviewed build stays unsupported exactly as an unrecognised release line does.

firstRunNotes: The new compaction smoke first failed at the resumed step. The cause was the harness, not OpenCode 2.1: it wrote its demand file once, the 15-second window expired mid-scenario and the observer correctly stopped tracking and cleared the chat. Renewing demand while the harness waits, as protocol-smoke.mjs already does, made the check pass with no companion change.

A diagnostic plugin added for that investigation whose setup never settled stalled the host's own plugin initialisation and made a later session read time out. Its setup now returns immediately and subscribes in the background. The tap records event shapes only and is read only by the SCOPE_SMOKE_DEBUG failure path.
limitations: Synthetic providers only: real token accounting, provider buffering, reasoning visibility and real workloads are not covered.
Stock OpenCode 2.1.1 and later 2.1 releases are accepted and self-checked but not qualified by this receipt; a self-check cannot detect changed meaning.
No live-host verification is included: this receipt says nothing about an ordinary Splash reply, prompt progress on the real provider, or the installed extension's UI.
The CPU fixture from companion-3.4.0.json was not re-run; 3.5.0 changes the accepted-version rule and the version string, not the event, storage or polling work it measured.
